profile.title: Bounded applicability
profile.canonical_definition: Principle that approaches have conditions under which they are useful and should not be treated as context-free universal solutions.
profile.summary: Bounded applicability says that a method or explanation earns validity within specified conditions rather than by being asserted as a context-free solution.
profile.why_it_matters: It is a useful antidote to method fundamentalism. It also imposes work: the boundary, evidence and transition conditions must be made explicit rather than invoked as a general escape clause.
common_misreadings: every claim is equally valid somewhere
open_checks: connect to affordances and context of use
profile.editorial_note: Developed from public primary, institutional, publisher and project sources. First-party source roles and independent evidential limits are stated explicitly.
